Hi Sophia —

Thanks for starting the onboarding — quick ask from procurement to keep this moving: we need a completed IRS W-9 (for US payees) with the EIN exactly as it appears on IRS records, plus the name and title of the person authorized to sign contracts/POs. Our AP team also requires a supporting EIN confirmation (CP575 or equivalent) and a copy of the authorized signer’s government ID (passport/driver’s license, redacted DOB ok).

If you can drop those as attachments or send a DocuSign envelope, we’ll validate the EIN and lift the PO hold. Target is to get PO issued this week so let us know if you have any constraints.

Attachments accepted: PDF W-9, EIN letter, signed authorization (electronic signature accepted)

Thanks,

Hi Sophia —

Thanks for sending these over. I ran the EIN through our verification check and there are two small issues to clear up before AP will activate the vendor record:

- Name/EIN exactness: the name on the W-9 appears as "Mica Software LLC" but the CP575 shows "Mica Labs, Inc." — we need confirmation of the legal name associated with EIN 12-3456789.
- Authorized signer proof: a signed W-9 is good, but for first-time vendors our policy requires either (a) a government-issued photo ID for the signer (we accept a redacted scan), or (b) a copy of Articles of Incorporation showing the CFO’s authority.

If you can reply with the corrected/certified W-9 that matches the EIN legal name and one of the two supporting documents above we’ll unblock the PO. If you prefer, DocuSign is fine — the envelope should include the completed W-9 and signer ID as an attachment.

Appreciate it —
Karthik
Senior Procurement Analyst
Redwood Inference

P.S. cc'ing Laura from Vendor Ops to align on the PO timeline.
